annotations.title: Save a new version of an automation

description: Saves a new version of one automation, named by id, from an automation document (ir) written in full, as Cosend’s automation editor saves one: what it starts on, its steps and its limits, in the document schema that ir_version names. What a document can use on a number, each trigger, step and integration action with what it takes, and that schema itself, are in the read-only list of automation building blocks for the number. The document is checked as it is saved; one that does not pass is refused with each failing path as a JSON pointer. A “Run a script” step runs TypeScript written in the step, in a sandbox with no network and nothing imported; an outside address is reached only by a step that calls an allowlisted URL. A document marked as made from a recipe (meta.created_by "recipe") is refused: a recipe is set up and changed with its own tools. The automation keeps running the version it ran until the new one is deployed and switched on. Each call needs confirming: without confirmation_token it changes nothing and returns a preview naming every action the document’s steps take, and a token for a person to approve; called again with that token, it saves. Returns the new version.

confirmation_token.description: For a call that needs approval: left out, the call does nothing and returns a preview and a token; given that token, with the same arguments, the call does it.

id.description: The id in the resource path.

ir.description: The automation’s flow document (the IR), as a JSON object. `ir_version` selects the document schema Cosend validates it against. A document that does not match is refused with `automation_invalid`, whose `error.details[]` names each failing path as a JSON pointer.

name: update_custom_automation
title: Save a new version of an automation
